title.suggested: Allen tried for keeping a disorderly house and discharged

summary.suggested: The St. Louis Post-Dispatch reported that Tom Allen was tried in Police Court for keeping a disorderly house, with police and a neighboring hotel keeper describing singing and fights, but Judge Cady discharged him.

metadata.notes: Masthead reads 'St. Louis Post-Dispatch Tuesday, October 30, 1883', page 2; item in the fourth column.

facts.fact: Allen was tried in the St. Louis Police Court on a charge of keeping a disorderly house at his saloon; Judge Cady found it not proved and discharged him. Cornelius McBride was his attorney
Allen's saloon adjoined the Metropolitan Hotel on Seventh Street between Chestnut and Market streets, whose proprietor Mr. Daly complained of the noise
places: Seventh Street between Chestnut and Market, St. Louis

notes: Saloon location is inferred: Daly's hotel rooms 'fronting on Allen's property'. The current title is a headline pun; a plainer title is suggested.
